ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=-x+1$ intersects with the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$. One of the intersection points has an abscissa of $-2$. After vertically translating the line $y=-x+1$ downwards by 2 units, find the coordinates of the intersection points between the translated line and the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} The graph of the linear function $y=-x+1$ is translated downward by 2 units to obtain $y=-x-1$,\\
by solving the system $\left\{\begin{array}{l}y=-\frac{6}{x}\\ y=-x-1\end{array}\right.$, we obtain: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=2 \\ y=-3\end{array}\right.$ or $\left\{\begin{array}{l}x=-3 \\ y=2\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of the intersections between the translated line and the graph of the hyperbolic function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ are $\boxed{\left(2，-3\right)}$ and $\boxed{\left(-3，2\right)}$.
